title: Correctness of a decider call
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ available deciders, let $D$ be a $k_D$-work-tape Boolean Turing machine, and choose its initial state for each decider. Suppose the initial program configuration is at state $l$, where the call specification selects decider $j$, a virtual input mode, an ordered list of register arguments, and the positive- and negative-answer successor states. Let $W$ assign a Boolean word to each register. Assume each argument register contains its assigned word on a tape initialized from cell zero, each such tape head is at zero, the argument registers are pairwise distinct, and the input head is at its initial position. If the selected decider, started on the virtual input formed from the call specification and the register words, halts with exactly the single output bit $b$, blank work tapes, work-tape heads returned to zero, and all work-tape head displacements bounded in absolute value by $B$ throughout the run, then the compiled machine has a time $T$ at which it reaches the original program configuration with the input head at its initial position and the control state set to the successor selected by $b$. At every time through $T$, each original register head remains in its prescribed region (outside the argument registers it stays at its initial position; on argument registers it lies between $-1$ and the word length), and each simulated decider work-tape head remains within distance $B$ of zero.
